newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul reopens bridge which collapsed killing 32.
newsitem.headline: Seoul reopens bridge which collapsed killing 32.

text.p: South Korea on Thursday reopened a bridge in central Seoul which collapsed two years ago, killing 32 people.
Witnesses said Seoul Mayor Cho Soon, relatives of the victims and religious leaders walked across the Songsu bridge before allowing cars to use it.

They threw 32 chrysanthemums into the Han river, which runs through Seoul, to remember the dead. In October 1994, a central span of the four-lane bridge plunged into the river taking with it cars, vans and a fully loaded bus during morning rush hour traffic.
City officials blamed shoddy workmanship for the disaster and vowed to end bribery which they said caused a reduction in essential spending needed for construction projects.
South Korea has been riddled with major man-made disasters, including a department store collapse which killed 502 people in 1995 and a construction site gas blast a year earlier that took 100 lives.
Last month the construction ministry revoked a licence to build steel-framed bridges for Dong Ah Construction Industrial Co Ltd, which built the Songsu bridge in 1979.
Hyundai Engineering and Construction Co Ltd, the largest local construction firm, rebuilt the bridge.
